ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — History and Physical — Sugar Ray Robinson — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Establishing care for memory loss and getting lost, with his care partner: cognitive testing, reversible causes, medicines, diabetes and blood pressure, driving and firearm safety

text.paragraph: Establishing care for memory loss and getting lost, with his care partner: cognitive testing, reversible causes, medicines, diabetes and blood pressure, driving and firearm safety [S]
This fictional modern episode addresses the presenting concerns below. [S]

list.item: He wants to know why he is forgetting and what can be done. [S]
He wants to keep his independence and keep working with the young fighters at the foundation. [S]
His care partner is worried about his driving and about managing alone. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: He was born Walker Smith Jr. on May 3, 1921. The Michigan Sports Hall of Fame gives his birthplace as Ailey, Georgia, with the family later moving to Detroit; the 1989 UPI obituary says he was born in Detroit. [D]
As a boy he moved with his family to Harlem in New York, and he won the Golden Gloves featherweight title in 1939. [D]
He held the world welterweight championship, won in 1946, and the world middleweight title five times, first in 1951. [D]

He boxed professionally from 1940 to 1965, about 200 bouts in all: the 1989 UPI obituary counts 201 fights, 109 won by knockout and 65 by decision; the 1987 UPI report gives a record of 174-19-6 and the Michigan Sports Hall of Fame 173-19-6. [D]

After boxing he settled in Los Angeles, living modestly in the top story of a duplex on West Adams Boulevard, and in 1969 founded the Sugar Ray Robinson Youth Foundation for inner-city children in the Los Angeles area. [D]
The project roster describes his dementia as probable boxing-related dementia pugilistica; no source read records that diagnosis, chronic traumatic encephalopathy, or an autopsy finding. [R]

text.paragraph: 4 later historical claims are omitted because they describe events after the index age. See the teaching note.
Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

list.item: Memory loss over about two years, worse in the past six months, with repeated questions, missed appointments and bills, and getting lost twice while driving in familiar streets, reported by him and his care partner; cause to be found: active, confirmed [S]
Type 2 diabetes for about ten years on metformin and glipizide; hemoglobin A1c 6.4%, below his goal, with hypoglycemia risk from the sulfonylurea: active, confirmed [S]
Hypertension, controlled on lisinopril: active, confirmed [S]

Dementia work-up under the Alzheimer's Association guideline: history from him and his care partner, MoCA, function, depression screening, first-tier blood tests (blood count, metabolic panel, B12, TSH), a review of medicines for anticholinergic and sedating drugs, a sleep apnea screen, and brain MRI. Guideline: Alzheimer's Association clinical practice guideline for the Diagnostic Evaluation, Testing, Counseling, and Disclosure of Suspected Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders (DETeCD-ADRD): Executive summary of recommendations for specialty care (2024); Alzheimer's Association clinical practice guideline for the Diagnostic Evaluation, Testing, Counseling, and Disclosure of Suspected Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders (DETeCD-ADRD): Executive summary of recommendations for primary care (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, Alzheimer's disease, diabetes type 2 and hypertension monographs (2026) [S]

Cognitive neurology consultation at the memory clinic to stage the dementia, weigh Alzheimer's disease against traumatic encephalopathy syndrome and vascular disease, choose biomarker testing, and decide anti-amyloid eligibility. Guideline: Alzheimer's Association clinical practice guideline for the Diagnostic Evaluation, Testing, Counseling, and Disclosure of Suspected Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders (DETeCD-ADRD): Executive summary of recommendations for specialty care (2024); Lecanemab: Appropriate Use Recommendations (2023); Donanemab: Appropriate use recommendations (2025); National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Traumatic Encephalopathy Syndrome (2021) [S]

Stop diphenhydramine, a strongly anticholinergic sleep aid; sleep habits and morning light instead. Guideline: American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults (2023) [S]

Driving: no driving until the evaluation is complete, with his care partner driving; firearm: unloaded and locked, with the key held by his care partner, until a decision with him. Guideline: Alzheimer's Association clinical practice guideline for the Diagnostic Evaluation, Testing, Counseling, and Disclosure of Suspected Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders (DETeCD-ADRD): Executive summary of recommendations for specialty care (2024); Practice Parameter update: Evaluation and management of driving risk in dementia (2010) [S]

Blood pressure under 130/80 mmHg on lisinopril, with potassium and creatinine checks. Guideline: CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, Alzheimer's disease, diabetes type 2 and hypertension monographs (2026); 13. Older Adults: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (2026) [S]

Advance care planning while he can take part fully: a health care agent and his values, at the preventive visit. Guideline: Alzheimer's Association clinical practice guideline for the Diagnostic Evaluation, Testing, Counseling, and Disclosure of Suspected Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders (DETeCD-ADRD): Executive summary of recommendations for specialty care (2024) [S]

Exercise, social activity and diabetes and blood pressure control as the brain-health measures with the most support. Guideline: Alzheimer's Association clinical practice guideline for the Diagnostic Evaluation, Testing, Counseling, and Disclosure of Suspected Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders (DETeCD-ADRD): Executive summary of recommendations for specialty care (2024); 13. Older Adults: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (2026) [S]
